stem: Which of the following clinical features is NOT typical of a facial nerve palsy:
fact: Eyelid elevation is supplied by levator palpebrae superioris via CN III and superior tarsal muscle via sympathetic fibres; facial palsy prevents closure, not elevation.
finding: Facial palsy affects eye closure, while eyelid elevation is not a CN VII function.

stem: Which of the following clinical features is NOT typical for a vagal nerve palsy:
options: Uvula deviation away from the affected side
Tongue deviation towards the affected side
fact: Tongue deviation toward the affected side indicates hypoglossal palsy, not vagal palsy.
mnemonic: X affects palate and voice; XII points the tongue.
finding: Vagal palsy causes palatal and laryngeal signs, while ipsilateral tongue deviation is CN XII.

stem: Regarding the glossopharyngeal nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: It is the efferent nerve of the gag reflex.
It emerges from the cranial cavity through the hypoglossal canal.
It carries taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.
It innervates the tensor veli palatini muscle.
It provides parasympathetic secretomotor fibres to the parotid gland.
fact: CN IX provides parasympathetic secretomotor fibres to the parotid gland and is the afferent gag limb.
mnemonic: IX tastes posteriorly and feeds the parotid.
finding: CN IX carries the parotid secretomotor pathway via the lesser petrosal nerve.

stem: Regarding the facial nerve, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: Forehead sparing in facial nerve palsy is indicative of a lower motor neuron lesion.
The facial nerve supplies taste to the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.
The facial nerve carries parasympathetic fibres to the lacrimal glands.
The facial nerve leaves the brainstem at the cerebellopontine angle.
The facial nerve exits the skull via the stylomastoid foramen.
fact: Forehead sparing indicates an upper motor neuron lesion; a lower motor neuron lesion involves the forehead.
mnemonic: UMN spares the forehead; LMN loses the whole side.
finding: Bilateral cortical input to the upper facial muscles explains forehead sparing in central lesions.

stem: Which of the following nerves is the afferent pathway of the pupillary light reflex:
fact: The optic nerve carries the afferent limb; CN III carries the parasympathetic efferent limb.
mnemonic: II sees the light; III constricts the pupil.
finding: The pupillary light reflex afferent pathway is carried by CN II.

stem: Regarding the accessory nerve, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: The nerve originates from cervical segments C1 - C5.
The nerve exits the skull through the jugular foramen.
The accessory nerve innervates the sternocleidomastoid and the trapezius muscle.
Accessory nerve palsy results in the inability to nod the head.
The nerve enters the cranial cavity through the foramen magnum.
fact: CN XI palsy impairs shoulder shrug and head rotation, not simple nodding.
mnemonic: XI shrugs and turns, not nods.
finding: The accessory nerve supplies sternocleidomastoid and trapezius and exits via jugular foramen.

stem: The abducens nerve innervates which of the following muscles:
fact: CN VI supplies lateral rectus, which abducts the eye.
mnemonic: LR6: lateral rectus by CN VI.
finding: The abducens nerve innervates lateral rectus.

stem: A 35 year old woman presents to ED complaining of an inability to shrug her left shoulder or to turn her head to face the right side. The most likely injured nerve causing her symptoms exits the skull through which of the following:
fact: Left CN XI injury weakens left trapezius and sternocleidomastoid; CN XI exits via the jugular foramen.
mnemonic: XI exits with IX and X through the jugular foramen.
finding: The accessory nerve exits the skull through the jugular foramen.

stem: A patient presents with an adducted eye at rest which cannot abduct past the midline, which of the following cranial nerves is most likely to be affected:
options: Ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve
fact: CN VI palsy leaves medial rectus unopposed, producing a convergent eye and impaired abduction.
finding: Abducens palsy causes a convergent squint and inability to abduct.

stem: A 50 year old man presents to ED with diplopia and a ptosis. On pulling his eyelid up, you note that his pupil is looking down and out, and his pupil is fixed and dilated. Further imaging shows that the patient has a cerebral aneurysm compressing a cranial nerve. Which of the following blood vessels is most likely to be the culprit:
fact: A posterior communicating artery aneurysm can compress the cisternal CN III, causing a pupil-involving oculomotor palsy.
finding: The cisternal oculomotor nerve lies near the posterior communicating artery.
